blackboard.known_findings: See ROADMAP.md. Settled with real numbers, do NOT re-test: the swing entry is statistically indistinguishable from random (8,203 trades); gross-of-cost expectancy ~0 so cheaper fills cannot rescue it; exit-model and stop-placement sweeps both negative; the simple daily strategy is beta not alpha; trade intensity as a filter does not improve net R/t. Order-flow research closed.
blackboard.live_features_needing_tests: (1) stopMode 'atr' — atrStopK and atrPeriod params control stop placement via trailing ATR, not raw swing low. Used in backtest.js and live scanner, never directly tested. (2) one-trade-per-level guard — same structural level (indexed by pivot candle) cannot fire twice; protects against re-entry whipsaw. Implemented in scanner.js, backtest.js handles it via levelOnCooldown. (3) alignment/trend gates on anticipate mode — MIN/MAX_STOP_PCT, chopFilter, trendGate, trendGateMode all apply in anticipate mode after a 2026-07-30 fix; prior tests only exercised BOS mode gates.

blackboard.queue_rule: Work ONE item per run, in order, smallest complete unit. Mark state done before moving on. If an item cannot be finished in one run, split it and add the remainder as a new item rather than leaving it half-built.

cost_policy.principle: Match effort to the job. The expensive part is reasoning, not tool calls - so the phase that needs judgement gets depth and the phase that needs a checklist gets brevity.
cost_policy.architect: RARE. Only when a genuinely new design decision exists. Routine queue advance needs no architect - the runner copies the next item mechanically.
cost_policy.executor: HEAVIEST and that is correct - this is where the actual work happens. Give it full effort.
cost_policy.verifier: BOUNDED AND CHEAP. Run npm test, compare the result against the item done_when, sanity-check any headline number for the classic failure (a big improvement resting on a tiny surviving sample). Do NOT re-derive the Executor work or re-run the research. Target a handful of tool calls, not a work session. Fail it back with reasoning if it smells wrong - a fast skeptical read is the job, a deep audit is not.
cost_policy.batching: Group queue items that touch the SAME FILE into one run. Three small tests in backtest.test.mjs is one coherent unit, not three - splitting them triples orient overhead (git pull + protocol + roadmap) and invites merge conflicts on one file.
cost_policy.orient_budget: Read AGENT_PROTOCOL.md and the ROADMAP tail once per run. Do not re-read the whole ROADMAP or re-explore the repo - the blackboard already carries what is settled.

blackboard.flow_data: EXTENDED BACKFILL COMPLETE. BTC/ETH/SOL order flow now spans 2026-01-01 -> 2026-07-29/30 (~2.3x the original window). This does NOT reopen the order-flow thread: intensity is dead on 11,195 independent samples across 20 pairs, and 15m imbalance is real (p=0.003) but worth only 1-6% of the 0.9% round-trip cost - more months cannot turn 1-6% into tradeable. Use this data only if a genuinely new aggressor-based feature is proposed.
blackboard.routing_rule: SELF-SERVE. The Architect is not in the routine loop - it was the bottleneck. Verifier on green marks the item done and pulls the next pending item into control in the SAME run, setting EXECUTOR_PENDING. Executor does the same if it finds its item already satisfied. Only set ARCHITECT_PENDING for a genuine design blocker (unspecified new file structure, objective contradicting the code, or work that would require touching a frozen path). Never idle waiting to be assigned.
blackboard.architect_duty: Keep this queue at 3+ pending items at all times so the Executor never blocks. Stocking ahead is the Architect job; approving individual pulls is not. If the queue drops below 3 pending, that is the signal to restock.
blackboard.pipeline: Architect -> Executor -> Verifier -> (next item) -> Executor. Every finished Executor item is automatically the Verifier next job, so the Executor keeps the Verifier busy just by finishing work. The Verifier pulls the next pending item in the SAME run it verifies, so the Executor is never idle either.

remediation_register.evidence: strategy.js exports global and per-timeframe stop/gate settings while scanner.js applies only selected constants; comments and active values require a live/backtest/docs parity audit.
remediation_register.risk: Operators and research can believe an inactive setting changes trading behavior or compare a non-equivalent backtest.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Classify each setting as active-live, active-research, deprecated, or experimental-disconnected and document intentional live/backtest differences.
acceptance_criteria: Every exported setting has one classification and executable behavior matches README/Discord/context claims.

remediation_register.evidence: trader.js:151-170 substitutes a quote when QueryOrders cannot confirm a sell, while monitor.js:309-310 removes the tracked position after placeSell returns.
remediation_register.risk: A timed-out, rejected, canceled, or unknown sell can be reported as closed and removed from monitoring while Kraken still holds the asset.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Require confirmed executed volume and terminal order status for sells; retain or precisely reduce tracked state otherwise and alert/reconcile.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown sell state never removes a tracked position.
Confirmed partial sell preserves the exact remaining volume.

remediation_register.evidence: monitor.js:35-40 stores manual halt only in process memory; bot.js:98-108 enables trading after restart when LIVE_TRADING=true, and commands.js:152-155 resumes without checking opt-in.
remediation_register.risk: A restart or owner typo can re-enable real orders despite a previously issued halt or the intended disabled-by-default posture.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Persist halt reason and gate resume on explicit environment opt-in plus healthy safety state.
acceptance_criteria: Manual/safety halt survives restart.
LIVE_TRADING false or unset cannot be overridden through Discord.

remediation_register.evidence: scanner.js:248 and monitor.js:361 use async work from independent invocations/setInterval without a single-flight guard.
remediation_register.risk: Slow Kraken/Discord calls can overlap scans or monitor ticks, causing duplicate work and race-prone state changes.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Use scoped single-flight guards and health telemetry for overlapping scan and monitor cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent invocation tests prove only one active scan/tick per loop and no duplicate order path.

remediation_register.evidence: storage.js has a hard-coded fallback Discord owner ID and bot/trader startup permits incomplete operational configuration with warnings.
remediation_register.risk: Misconfigured deployment can expose owner controls or start a process whose safety assumptions are not explicit.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Require explicit production owner/live configuration, redact errors, test authorization, and document least-privilege credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Unconfigured owner cannot authorize trading.
No log path emits credentials or token material.

remediation_register.evidence: bot.js only logs uncaughtException/unhandledRejection and has no shutdown protocol; software exits rely on the running monitor.
remediation_register.risk: A corrupted process can continue or terminate without a clear halt/recovery signal.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Halt entries, persist/reveal unsafe state, and terminate/restart through a reconciled boot path on fatal conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Fatal/shutdown tests prove no new entry and explicit recovery requirements.

remediation_register.evidence: Kraken calls have inconsistent retry behavior; price and sell-fill fallbacks can treat unavailable remote state as usable local data.
remediation_register.risk: Network failures can produce stale pricing, ambiguous orders, and incorrect tracked positions.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Introduce bounded request policies and explicit unknown states at every order-critical API boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Timeout/exhaustion never produces a trade or an inferred fill.

remediation_register.evidence: Discord login/lifecycle failure handling is absent.
remediation_register.risk: Scans can start without a healthy Discord lifecycle.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Handle login/lifecycle failure before scan startup.
acceptance_criteria: Failed Discord readiness starts no scan or entry.

remediation_register.evidence: DATA_DIR silently falls back to cwd despite durable position-state requirements.
remediation_register.risk: Ephemeral storage can lose exit-management state.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Gate live readiness on durable storage preflight.
acceptance_criteria: Unsafe storage cannot enable orders.

remediation_register.evidence: swarm-runner has no execution lease and stages all files.
remediation_register.risk: Concurrent runners can duplicate work or commit another agent's changes.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Add scoped staging and exclusive lease.
acceptance_criteria: A second runner dispatches nothing; unrelated paths never commit.

remediation_register.evidence: Candle ingestion/cache resampling lack strict validation, corruption recovery, and provenance.
remediation_register.risk: Research can silently use fabricated, incomplete, or irreproducible inputs.
remediation_register.proposed_resolution: Validate candles, rebuild corrupt caches, and fingerprint content/spec/code.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid data is excluded and every result records deterministic provenance.

remediation_register.evidence: npm audit --omit=dev reports high production vulnerabilities.
remediation_register.risk: Known vulnerable dependency chain remains deployed.
acceptance_criteria: No unaccepted high production audit finding remains.

budget.observed_usage_at_set: 88% of the 5h window consumed at 2026-07-30T20:28Z (reported by the human). ~12% headroom, so roughly 35 minutes equivalent.
budget.sizing_rationale: Extended on explicit human instruction to keep going (they are monitoring quota and will call the pause). Prior 2-run/30-min cap would have expired before the 30-minute cron ever fired, disabling the loop having done zero work - a cap that stops the loop before it starts is not a safety feature, it is a bug. 6 runs x 30min = 3h of cron opportunities inside a 2h clock, so the clock is the binding constraint and the run count is headroom.
budget.on_exhausted: Set control.status PAUSED_BUDGET, append a ledger entry, DISABLE the scheduled task cajh-swarm-loop via update_scheduled_task(enabled:false), then exit doing nothing else.
budget.resume_after_reset: When the 5h window resets: set runs_used 0, push expires_at forward, raise max_runs (8 is reasonable on a fresh window), set control.status back to EXECUTOR_PENDING, re-enable the task.

timing_observed.one_executor_run: Q1 (3 specified tests, delivered 4) consumed ~1 loop run and finished inside a single cron slot. Cost was material - roughly the same order as several architect turns.
timing_observed.why: 30 minutes was far too aggressive. It fires faster than a substantive Executor task completes, so runs stack up and quota drains with little marginal progress. A 2-hour cadence gives one task room to finish, be verified, and hand off cleanly before the next fire - and 12 runs/day instead of 48 is a ~4x reduction in idle-run overhead.
timing_observed.guidance_for_resume: Match cadence to task size, not to impatience. Heavy items (walkforward.mjs, funding analysis) deserve 2h+. Light items (doc passes, small test additions) could run hourly. If a run ever finds the previous task still unfinished, the cadence is too fast - widen it rather than letting runs pile up.

resume_on_reset.purpose: Everything the loop needs to restart cold, with no human explanation. Follow it top to bottom.
preflight: 2. npm test -> expect 11 passing. If not, STOP and set control.status BLOCKED; a red baseline means something upstream broke and no new work should land on it.
3. Confirm working tree is clean (git status). Uncommitted work from a killed run must be inspected and committed BEFORE new work starts, never discarded.

reset_budget.note: 8 runs at a 2h cadence is 16h of opportunities inside a 4h clock, so the clock binds and the run count is headroom.

first_task.note: Copy this items file/task into control.target_file/control.objective, set control.status EXECUTOR_PENDING, control.iteration 0, and mark the item started. Do NOT wait for the Architect - the spec is complete.

resume_on_reset.reenable: Re-enable the scheduled task: update_scheduled_task taskId cajh-swarm-loop, enabled true. Cron is already 0 */2 * * * (2h) which matches observed task duration - do not shorten it without evidence.
resume_on_reset.executor_ready: Q2 (funding.mjs collector) is fully specified and needs no design: public Kraken Futures endpoint, three symbols, CSV per symbol, idempotent merge, print rows+span. It is deliberately collector-only so it cannot sprawl.
resume_on_reset.verifier_ready: The Verifier has work the moment the Executor finishes anything: run npm test, check the item done_when, look for the classic failure (a big improvement resting on a tiny surviving sample, or a decile spread with no monotonic relationship). Then mark done and pull the next pending item in the SAME run so the Executor is never idle.
resume_on_reset.invariants: Live trading stays OFF. Frozen paths unchanged (backtest.test.mjs is the sole assignable exception). Never checkout/reset/stash another agents work. Never kill node processes or touch candles/. Commit before advancing status. Statistical claims need non-overlapping samples + block permutation + BH-FDR + a cost comparison - every borderline result here has died under those.
